paper_title: Computing Optimal Regularizers for Online Linear Optimization
authors: Khashayar Gatmiry, Jon Schneider, Stefanie Jegelka
statement: Of course, it is possible that there is a method for computing the optimal regularizer that sidesteps the need to be able to verify the convexity of an arbitrary regularizer – we leave this as an interesting open problem.
context: The proof of Theorem 12 is provided in Section G.5. At a high level, Theorem 12 asserts that there exists a distribution over norm balls L such that (1) even exp(d1−ϵ ) queries are insufficient to 1 distinguish between L and the Euclidean unit ball, while (2) the Identity Hessian is not α = d1−ϵ strongly convex with respect to the dual norm ∥.∥Lc . Of course, it is possible that there is a method for computing the optimal regularizer that sidesteps the need to be able to verify the convexity of an arbitrary regularizer – we leave this as an interesting open problem. 12 C OMPUTING O PTIMAL R EGULARIZERS
